ideas.title: Fire that spreads through whatever it touches
ideas.goal: The player lights fires on purpose (a campfire to cook fish, coals for the kiln, a hot wire in dry grass) and has to keep them from spreading: dig sand into a firebreak, wet the grass from the pond, drag the stool away. Wind shifts, a spark jumps, a wooden fence catches and sags. Fun: every fire is a small fight you can win or lose, and the island remembers it (char, ash, a burnt stump).
ideas.toward: 'Thin wire heats and melts' and the heat every smelting and circuit step needs, as one general system: anything with fuel burns by what it is.
ideas.idea: Each prop and part carries a temperature, a fuel mass and its material's ignition point, burn rate and heat of combustion. Burning things heat their neighbours by radiation (falling with distance and seen area) and by contact, tilted by the wind; a prop past its ignition point catches; fuel burns away, the mass drops, and a wooden part's strength drops with its char depth, so a burning fence or bench sags and breaks under its own weight. Water takes heat away and leaves wet fuel that won't catch until it dries. The grass is cells of the same kind, so the meadow carries it too. Watching: a ring of flame creeping out from a glowing wire, a gust pushing it at the fence, the fence sagging and falling in, friends running to the pond.
ideas.form: An engine heat-and-combustion system over props and grass (GPU kernels over the prop list), fire and smoke drawn as real emissive volumes in the path tracer; a dusk film of a fire that gets away.

ideas.title: Catch the lightning
ideas.goal: When a storm comes the player plants copper rods and runs wire down into the wet sand; the bolt's branching path is grown through the field those conductors shape, so the player learns to steer it: away from the cottage, into a rod, or on purpose into a tree. Where it lands it burns, and in dry sand it leaves a glass root you dig up, shaped by your setup. Fun: guessing where the next one strikes, protecting things, collecting the strange glass.
ideas.toward: Real fields deciding what happens: the same Laplace field solve and conductors from the materials table, at a scale nobody can fake.
ideas.idea: A dielectric breakdown model (Niemeyer-Pietronero-Wiesmann): solve Laplace's equation on a 3D grid between the cloud base and the ground, with every conductor (rods, wire, wet ground, trees by water content) held at ground potential; the channel grows step by step to neighbours with probability by field strength to a power, so it branches like real lightning and finds the rods. The strike's energy goes into the heat system: trees catch, sand above its melting point along the channel becomes a glass mesh. Watching: a branching bolt lighting the whole island blue-white for a frame, snapping into Lumi's rod instead of the roof; next morning Lumi digging out a forked glass root.
ideas.form: A GPU Laplace + growth solver (Mantle kernels), the bolt as an emissive tube and a light in the path tracer, a storm plugin hook; a storm film.

ideas.title: A lamp that lasts the night
ideas.goal: The player makes a lamp for the dark cottage: picks a filament (copper wire, iron wire, a charred grass stalk), its thickness, and whether it sits in open air or under a glass jar where a candle first burned up the air. Too thin flashes and dies, too thick barely glows, in air it burns through in seconds. Fun: experimenting until a lamp burns all night and the cottage glows warm for the friends.
ideas.toward: A circuit that does something people need, from the cells and wire on the road; the path tracer's light comes from what the player built.
ideas.idea: Filament resistance from material, length and section; Joule power against radiation and convection gives its temperature; the colour and brightness are blackbody at that temperature and drive a real light in the scene; oxidation eats the filament at a rate by temperature and the oxygen left in the jar (a candle inside uses it up first); thinning raises the resistance until it breaks. Watching: the cottage interior lit only by a little orange coil, friends gathering, then a flicker and dark when the first try burns out.
ideas.form: Circuit + filament physics, a lamp-making bench plugin, the lamp as an emissive light lighting the cottage; a night film inside the cottage.

ideas.title: The eel in the pond is a battery
ideas.goal: An eel lives in the pond and stuns the fish it hunts. The player can watch fish twitch near it, then lay copper wires into the water to catch its current, enough to make a lamp flicker or Lumi's crest stand up, and has to keep it fed and calm to keep the power on. Fun: a living power source with moods, figuring out where in the water the wire picks up the most.
ideas.toward: Cells in series (an eel is thousands of them) and a field in a conductor: electricity from a creature instead of a stone.
ideas.idea: The eel's electric organ as a stack of cells with an internal resistance, firing in bursts when it hunts or is bothered; the pond water as a conductor where the field around the eel follows from a current-dipole solution, so a fish or a wire tip feels a voltage by where it is and how it lies. Fish twitch by that voltage, the eel's hunting behaviour uses it. Watching: a dark eel coiling round a fish that jerks still; Lumi's two wires in the water, a lamp on the bank flickering in time with the eel's bursts.
ideas.form: A new creature with its own behaviour plus a field-in-water solver; plugin at the pond; a film from the bank.
